VERDICT: EXTEND C0004 | FIND — `scan_health()` not only misreports missing binaries as available; it also misreports tool timeouts as available. Evidence: `_run_tool()` returns `CompletedProcess(..., returncode=-1, stderr="TIMEOUT")` on timeout, but `run_pyright/run_ruff/run_bandit/run_mypy` only special-case `"NOT_FOUND"` and otherwise return `[]`. `scan_health()` treats any normal return from the runner as success and sets `tools_available[tool_name] = True`. FOLLOW — a hung analyzer is reported as healthy/available, so the insect brain receives a false clean bill of health rather than degraded observability. That can suppress operator attention to dead scans and make fix-evaluation baselines look like “0 issues” instead of “tool failed”. FIX — same root-cause fix as C0004/C0001: propagate execution status from `_run_tool`/runner and mark tools unavailable on timeout as well as not-found.

VERDICT: CONFIRM C0014

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.94
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.62
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not evaluate fixes in a real sandbox for tools that depend on project/module context. It copies only the single target file to a temp directory, but computes post-fix diagnostics by running `run_pyright`, `run_ruff`, and `run_bandit` on that lone copied file (`patched_path`). Evidence: `patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))` and then `_count_tool_issues(run_pyright, patched_path)` etc. For imports, sibling modules, package layout, pyright config, and relative paths, the temp file is no longer in the original repository structure. This violates the stated contract “sandbox-test proposed fixes” because many fixes will be judged against an invalid isolated environment rather than the actual codebase context.
FOLLOW: Downstream, fix verification can silently produce wrong SAFE/HARMFUL/NEUTRAL verdicts. A patch that breaks imports or package interfaces may look SAFE because the isolated single-file run no longer sees cross-file errors; conversely a valid patch may look harmful/unevaluable because project context vanished in the tempdir. The immune pipeline consumes these verdicts in Stage 4 and marks findings `verified=True` when verdict is SAFE/NEUTRAL. That crosses the interface into `immune_agents.py` bug-closing logic: a wrongly verified fix can close the bug in subsequent rounds and suppress further review, which is a high-severity silent misclassification in the PoC happy path.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — when sandboxing, copy the full relevant source tree (at minimum all `source_paths`, preserving relative paths) into the temp directory, patch the target file at its corresponding relative location, and run post-fix tools from that sandbox root instead of against a lone basename copy.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` can execute tests against the wrong codebase, including the unmodified real repository, despite claiming sandboxed fix evaluation. Evidence: after writing the patched file into `tmpdir`, it runs `_run_tool(test_cmd, cwd=tmpdir)`, but `test_cmd` is passed through unchanged. In the actual interface from `immune_agents.py`, the command is `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", "-x", "-q", "--tb=no", "--no-header", "-q"]`. With `cwd=tmpdir`, `bench/tests/` usually does not exist in the sandbox because only one file was copied; Python and pytest can then resolve imports/tests from outside the tempdir via the interpreter path and current environment, meaning the test run is not bound to the patched sandbox.
FOLLOW: This breaks the core guarantee “no source modification / sandbox-test proposed fixes” at the behavioral level: test results may reflect the original repository instead of the patched candidate. A bad patch can be labeled SAFE because tests exercised unmodified source; a good patch can fail because the sandbox lacks the test tree. Those verdicts feed back into immune Stage 4 verification and bug-closed gating, so the system can wrongly verify or reject fixes and mislead the reviewer about whether the proposed correction was actually tested.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — stage the repo subset needed for testing into the temp directory (source files plus referenced test paths), and rewrite/validate `test_cmd` so every filesystem path points inside that sandbox before execution; if that cannot be done, skip tests and mark them not run rather than executing against ambient real-repo paths.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.53
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` can classify a fix as `SAFE` even when it introduces new issues in one tool, as long as reductions in other tools make the summed net negative. Evidence: it computes `total_net = net_type_errors + net_ruff_errors + net_bandit_issues`; `HARMFUL` only if `total_net > 0`, `SAFE` if `total_net < 0`. Example from the code’s own metrics: a patch with `+3` new bandit issues and `-5` ruff issues yields `total_net = -2`, so verdict becomes `SAFE` even though security regressions were introduced.
FOLLOW: Downstream this is a silent wrong result in the fix-evaluation feature. The immune pipeline treats SAFE/NEUTRAL as grounds to set `finding.verified=True`. Because the verdict collapses distinct defect classes into a single sum, a patch can worsen security or type safety and still close the bug if cosmetic/style reductions outweigh it numerically. That directly corrupts the “first verified fix wins” mechanism and can suppress further review of a genuinely harmful patch.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — mark a fix `HARMFUL` if any individual net field is positive (`net_type_errors > 0 or net_ruff_errors > 0 or net_bandit_issues > 0`); only classify as SAFE when no category regresses and at least one improves or tests pass.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.74
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.41
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_apply_fix_to_source()` can falsely treat arbitrary multi-line valid Python snippets as whole-file replacements, regardless of whether they correspond to the finding or preserve surrounding file content. Evidence: after failing search-replace, it does `compile(fix, "<fix>", "exec")` and if `fix.count("\n") >= 5`, returns `fix` as the entire new source. Any prose-free code block with 6+ lines qualifies, even if it is only a helper function or partial patch. This makes “apply fix” succeed by replacing the entire file with an unrelated fragment.
FOLLOW: Downstream fix evaluation becomes misleading rather than conservative. A malformed or partial suggestion can be turned into a full-file overwrite in the sandbox, producing arbitrary tool counts and possibly SAFE/NEUTRAL verdicts unrelated to the intended fix. Because immune Stage 4 relies on these verdicts to verify fixes, the system can programmatically bless a nonsensical patch format instead of correctly treating it as unevaluable.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — remove the implicit whole-file replacement heuristic; only allow whole-file replacement when the proposed fix is explicitly marked as a full file body, otherwise return `None` unless a concrete search/replace or line-targeted patch applies.
VERIFIED: TRUE
